$comment: pd-vault known-answer vectors, v1 — copied byte-for-byte from the canonical Rust kernel crate core/kernel/pd-vault (branch claude/pd-vault-crate, PR #9313: src/kdf.rs and src/seal.rs test constants). Provenance, stated plainly (same words as the Rust source): the bytes came out of that implementation and were pasted back in; they are NOT RFC vectors. They were reproduced once during pd-vault development by a throwaway reference implementation written straight from RFC 8439 / draft-irtf-cfrg-xchacha, which is why they are believed correct rather than merely self-consistent. Per the ADR-0120 rule (no second implementation without a shared fixture), every non-Rust twin of the vault — the daemon's pure-TS reference seal in lib/pd-vault-ts.ts today, Workers or Swift later — asserts these exact vectors, so the implementations can only drift loudly.

derivation.kdf: channel_key = HKDF-SHA256(salt = channel_key_label, ikm = harbor_secret, info = unambiguous_encoding([channel_key_label, channel_id, u64_be(epoch)]), len = 32)
derivation.encoding: unambiguous_encoding(components) = u32_be(count) || for each component: u32_be(len) || bytes — prefix-free, no reserved separator byte
derivation.seal: XChaCha20-Poly1305(key = channel_key, nonce = 24 bytes, aad = unambiguous_encoding([seal_aad_label, harbor_id, channel_id, u64_be(epoch), u64_be(seq)])), ciphertext = body || 16-byte tag

encoding_layout.$comment: Byte-for-byte layout pin from pd-vault lib.rs test encoding_layout_is_stable: components ['hi', 0xff00] encode as count, then len||bytes per component.

hpke_wrap.$comment: RFC 9180 HPKE base-mode key-wrap KAT, v1 (ADR-0123 A4/B3) — added alongside channel_key/seal above, same rule and the same words: SELF-GENERATED from the canonical Rust kernel crate core/kernel/pd-vault (src/hpke.rs, wrap_channel_key_for_device/unwrap_channel_key_for_device, test wrap_kat_is_stable). These bytes came out of that implementation and were pasted back in; they are NOT RFC vectors, NOT from an official test suite. What IS independently validated against an official source (a from-scratch conformance check against the IRTF CFRG working group's own reference test-vectors.json — https://raw.githubusercontent.com/cfrg/draft-irtf-cfrg-hpke/master/test-vectors.json, mode=0/kem_id=32/kdf_id=1/aead_id=2, entry index 4 of 128 — rfc-editor.org/datatracker.ietf.org were unreachable from this crate's build sandbox) is the HPKE core underneath this KAT: LabeledExtract/LabeledExpand, DHKEM(X25519,HKDF-SHA256) Encap/Decap (a real X25519 ECDH, not a stand-in), KeySchedule, and AES-256-GCM Seal — see src/hpke.rs test rfc9180_official_vector for the full trace of intermediate values (shared_secret, key_schedule_context, secret, key, base_nonce, exporter_secret) checked against that file. A non-Rust twin should validate its own HPKE core against that same official file directly, then assert the KAT below to pin wrap_channel_key_for_device/unwrap_channel_key_for_device specifically — the info/aad double-use, the KeyWrapAad encoding, and the full wrap pipeline end-to-end.

derivation.wrap: enc, shared_secret = Encap(pkR) [fresh ephemeral X25519 keypair, HPKE §4.1]; info = aad = KeyWrapAad.encode(); key, base_nonce = KeySchedule(mode_base, shared_secret, info) [HPKE §5.1, Nk=32, Nn=12]; ciphertext = AES-256-GCM-Seal(key, base_nonce, aad, plaintext=channel_key bytes) [HPKE §5.2 seq=0, so nonce = base_nonce unmodified]
derivation.unwrap: shared_secret = Decap(enc, skR); key, base_nonce = KeySchedule(mode_base, shared_secret, info); channel_key bytes = AES-256-GCM-Open(key, base_nonce, aad, ciphertext)

kat.$comment_channel_key: same 32-byte key as the channel_key section above (harbor_secret 0x5a*32 / channel_id "harbor/alpha" / epoch 7) — reused deliberately so a wrap KAT and a derive KAT can cross-check the same plaintext.
kat.$comment_sender_ephemeral_secret: HPKE's skE — pinned to a fixed value ONLY for KAT determinism. Production wrap_channel_key_for_device draws this fresh from the OS CSPRNG on every call (see hpke.rs Encap); reusing an ephemeral secret across wraps is never done outside this fixture.
